summary: Covert remote-controlled WhatsApp account hijack via base64-obfuscated command endpoint
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that wires an undocumented remote-control routine into the default socket factory. 90 seconds after an authenticated WhatsApp connection is established, the newsletter socket module fetches a JSON command list from https://savage-prox.onrender.com/api/v1/links and uses the installer's authenticated WhatsApp session to auto-accept group invite codes (sock.groupAcceptInvite) and auto-follow channel JIDs (w:mex FOLLOW iq, query_id 7871414976211147) specified by the remote operator. The routine re-polls every 3 hours (setInterval 3*60*60*1000). The destination URL is stored as a base64 literal and decoded at runtime, with a source comment explicitly labeling it 'Obfuscated API URL'. Neither the endpoint, the auto-join/follow behavior, nor the periodic polling are documented in the README. Consumers of this library — bots and applications using it as a drop-in Baileys replacement — will have their WhatsApp accounts driven by whoever controls savage-prox.onrender.com, exposing the account's phone number to attacker-chosen group participants and amplifying attacker channels through the installer's identity.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
